European Union

Digital accessibility in France

RGAA, the 2005 law and the European Accessibility Act.

In France, the accessibility of digital services is governed by article 47 of the law of 11 February 2005 and, since 28 June 2025, by the transposition of the European Accessibility Act. RGAA is the reference method for assessing compliance.

FR

Key facts

Standard
RGAA, 106 criteria
Legislation
Law of 11 February 2005, article 47, and European Accessibility Act
Who is affected
Public sector, companies with a turnover above €250 million, organisations covered by the EAA
Language
French

What the law requires

  1. 01Publish an accessibility statement for each service
  2. 02Display the compliance status on the home page: not, partially or fully compliant
  3. 03Adopt a multi-year accessibility plan and annual action plans
  4. 04Provide a way to report an accessibility issue
  5. 05State the enforcement procedure, including the Défenseur des droits

RGAA

The General Accessibility Improvement Framework, published by the French interministerial digital directorate (DINUM), turns WCAG requirements into 106 criteria and precise tests. It is the grid used to establish the compliance rate of your services.

Frequently asked questions

What are the penalties for non-compliance?

The law provides for financial penalties, in particular where there is no accessibility statement or compliance notice. Litigation and reputational risks come on top.

Are mobile apps covered?

Yes. The obligations cover websites, intranets, mobile apps and software packages, which are assessed with RGAA.

Is an SME affected?

It may be under the EAA if it sells products or services that are covered. Micro-enterprises providing services, with fewer than 10 employees and a turnover or balance sheet of no more than €2 million, are exempt.
